subject: telescope
pitch: A brass explorer's telescope on a wooden tripod. A long tube in polished brass with leather-wrapped sections and engraved rings, a smaller finder scope on top, an eyepiece with a rubber cup, focusing knobs, and a mahogany tripod with brass fittings and a little tray holding a rolled star chart.
reasoning:
Since I don't have the full API docs, I need to work carefully within the reference I do have, designing a model using the builder's joint, chain, sweep, part, stick, ring, and extrude functions along with painting and stripe utilities.

For the telescope prop, I'm thinking of keeping things simple since it's mostly static geometry rather than a creature — using a root joint with parts attached for the tripod head and tube pivot, while being cautious about how `b.part` orients geometry (whether through `at`, `aim`, `dir`, or manual rotation) since I'm not fully certain of the signature.

I'm sketching proportions now: roughly 1.5m tripod height, 0.8m telescope length, centered at origin and facing +Z. For the legs, I'm leaning toward either tapered cylinders rotated to connect the head point to each foot, or using `b.sweep` with a simple two-point path and a radius to create a thin rod shape, though I'm unsure how `b.sweep` behaves with just two points.

I'm planning the telescope tube as a brass sweep along the z-axis, with leather-wrapped sections as slightly larger overlapping sweeps and thin dark cylinders for engraved decorative rings. The finder scope will be a smaller parallel sweep mounted on brackets above the main tube, with a dark glass objective lens cap at the front and knurled focusing knobs built from small rotated cylinders, plus a tripod head joint connecting everything at the top.

For the tripod mount, I'll tilt the whole tube assembly up at a 40-degree angle by computing a direction vector and placing points along it mathematically, then sweeping between those points for both the tube and its leather/ring details — avoiding the need for orientation frames since everything's just point-to-point sweeps. Knobs can be simple spheres placed at the right coordinates.

Now I'm planning the rest of the telescope's accessories: a small tray with a rolled parchment chart (skipping risky texture APIs for safety), three mahogany tripod legs splayed out from the head to the feet with a wooden spreader ring connecting them at mid-height, and brass fittings at the leg tops and head block using simple cylinder and box geometries since those don't need rotation.

Setting up the main tube geometry along a defined direction vector, with segments for the brass tube body, leather grip wraps, engraved decorative rings, the objective lens cell and glass at the front, and the eyepiece barrel with rubber eyecup at the rear. I'm also positioning a small finder scope offset above the main tube using a perpendicular vector, connected by small mounting brackets.

Now I'm adding the focus knobs on the tube's side using rotated cylinders, then building the cradle/trunnion mount that holds the tube, and finally laying out the tripod head and three splayed legs with feet positioned at 120-degree angle intervals around the base.

Mapping out the leg collars, rubber feet, central hub, and wooden spreader bars connecting the legs at their midpoints, then placing a small accessory tray at the spreader's center for holding eyepieces.

For support, I'm adding a thin brass rod running down from the hub to the tray, reading visually as a tripod center column. I'm also sketching a rolled star chart on the tray as a small sweep cylinder with a thin red ribbon band, then considering what minimal skeleton joints the model needs -- settling on adding a basic "head" joint since props seem allowed without an elaborate rig.

Deciding to skip joints and keep bones auto-assigned by proximity instead, since simple parts attached to the root should work fine. Now I'm starting to write the actual module code, defining the color palette (brass, leather, wood, rubber, glass, paper, red) before building out the tripod legs and other geometry.

Setting up tilt angle and direction vectors for the telescope's axis, then defining helper functions to compute points along that axis with offsets for sweeps and part placement. Working through how knobs and buttons should be rotated so their cylinder axis sits perpendicular to the tube direction, positioning them along the tilted barrel.

Still working out finder scope and bracket geometry...

Now I'm setting up the cradle trunnion along the X-axis through the tube center, then adding a simplified head yoke with a brass block connecting down to the trunnion.

Working out the tripod: three legs at 120° spacing with feet touching the ground, brass ferrule collars near the tops, rubber-tipped feet, and a central hub joining them. I'm placing a center column down to a wooden accessory tray with raised rim boxes, adding a triangular spreader bar between the legs at mid-height, and tucking a rolled star chart with a red binding band onto the tray—carefully working out all the Y-coordinates so the tray, rim, roll, and column all align without gaps or overlaps.

I'm double-checking the overall proportions so the telescope tube, trunnion, finder scope, and tripod head all sit at consistent heights relative to each other, keeping the total assembly around 1.5 units tall.

Now I'm finalizing the helper function that converts tube-local offsets (along axis, up, and side) into world coordinates, then writing out the main tube sweep, cradle block, brass knob, and leg-building loop using that helper, plus the objective lens cell and glass disc, making sure everything compiles cleanly as TypeScript using only the builder SDK before returning the completed root object.
